There should be a straightforward way of disabling downvotes aside from using CSS to hide the buttons. The CSS trick has two major problems: It's way more complicated than it needs to be, and it is easy to get around if you are determined to downvote something. Subverses should be able to easily disable downvotes by clicking a check box and this should apply even when subverse styles are disabled or when a post is viewed outside the subverse, e.g. on the front page. I think this would be a great addition to the settings moderators have access to for their subverses and would strongly benefit voat.
Allow mods to disable downvotes in their subverses
Disallowing downvoats would probably break the ranking. Compared to posts/comments with downvoats, "downvoat-castrated" posts/comments look like a post/comment where everyone agrees on.
Not if people understand downvotes were disabled. Then it looks like nobody downvoted because they're not able to.

My concerns are not the users but the scripts who decide what to show on the front page and how to sort comments. How sould they compare the ratings? I can't think of a fair algorythm for merging dovnvoatable and undownvoatable posts; that doesn't mean it's not possible, but it's likely not trivial.

That's a good point. I'm not sure how to deal with that aside from maybe just deducting a few points from a post while deciding its ranking to account for downvotes being disabled, though that may or may not work well.

Here are some options I have thought about:

  • Don't list them at all: This would be too drastic IMHO
  • List them seperately: not user friendly
  • Multiply score with average upvoat/downvoat rate: Subvoats with below average rate could disable downvoats to get better score
  • Multiply score with worst upvoat/downvoat rate: Probably similar to not listing at all
  • Multiply score with some hardcoded or admin set value: intransparent and how would the score be decided on

I'm open to new ideas while also believing in the power of downvoats. I dislike the facebook strategy of valueing posts high because a few like them a lot and the superiority hates them.

However, before searching I did search if somebody posted it already and have found that a similar submission was here some months ago and was already implemented. It seems this way to donate via cryptocurrency was removed due the fears of users giving the wrong impression to this site.

Here is what I think about it. Who is actually in control of this site right now? Does the owner, Atko, excluding the website costs itself, have real, working, staff that they are paying right now? Or are they at the moment simply volunteers? These add up to the costs.

It could be possible to implement a bar that shows the current server costs with the absolute cost of running the server and a percentage and a way to verify that this is really the value at that bar. This adds trust for the users.

Donation can be through many means, and what should really be considered is cryptocurrency. When this percentage exceeds 100% this goes to the living costs of the owner and everyone involved. Nothing is truly free, and the maintainers need to get the sources to maintain it (and themselves). And indeed, if this site cannot be maintained, it will collapse. You might say that somebody else can fork voat if that happens, but then again unless that owner can sustain themselves through other means it will still suffer the same problem. If the owner of this site is planning to sacrifice their job and to devote their time to this site then there must be a way to sustain that kind of living.

It seems there is also a search for investors for Voat. Investors, if they have share of the "company" unless they are the "Yes, I will risk this money for you and it doesn't matter if my investment falls" variety, can sway the direction this site through good or bad means. I would suggest to postpone this search and test this "crowd-driven means of donation" while this site's maintenance costs are not atmospheric yet a bit if it has not started, and see if this method words at the time being. If unsustainable, then ideas that have been picked over time can be started.
